html:
SMTO-MEM-0043 — Knowledge's document helper stopped responding

GUID: 01e08c6d-364c-5835-a70f-4c5146987342
Slug: knowledge-worker-unavailable
Domain: MEM · Subsystem: knowledge

What happened

  • Knowledge uses a helper program to read documents and prepare them for search. It stopped responding or took too long on this work, so the work was stopped. SMTO starts a fresh helper next time.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Knowledge. If the document shows Indexing failed, select Retry failed jobs, or open Manage on its card and select Reindex. SMTO starts a fresh helper for the next attempt, which often clears a one-time stall.
  2. If the same large document fails again, split it into smaller files, or ask your administrator to raise Processing timeout (seconds) on the Document settings tab in Knowledge. Very large or complex documents can take longer than the time allowed.
  3. Open System Health and select Check Knowledge. This shows whether the Knowledge installation is damaged rather than just slow.
  4. If the check fails, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. A damaged installation must be repaired on the server.

What success looks like

  • The document moves through indexing to Ready to search.

If it still fails

  • Send the copied error details to the person who manages SMTO, naming the document and its size. Don't delete the document; it is kept and can be indexed after the repair.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • WorkerClient.call lost the Knowledge processing worker: writing the request failed (broken pipe or OS error) or no answer arrived before the processing timeout, so the worker was closed.

What this means

  • The app could not use an indexing worker for this request. The installation and failed job need inspection. The original operation and completed work retain their own recorded outcomes; this diagnostic does not replay them.

Why this can happen

  • The component reported worker_unavailable. This does not establish the outcome of unrelated operations.

How to diagnose it

  • The affected job advances through indexing to Ready.
  • Inspect the error reference and the affected component’s current observation before selecting a recovery action.

How to fix it

  • Retry the job (Reindex or Retry failed jobs); the next call starts a new worker process. If it recurs, run Check Knowledge on System Health to verify the installation, compare the document against “Processing timeout (seconds)” and “Maximum ingestion time (seconds)”, and check the server for the worker being killed; repair with python -m agent_runtime.rag.install if verification fails.
  • Open System Health to check Knowledge dependencies. Ask an administrator to repair the installation if verification fails, then retry the affected indexing job.

Retry and execution caution

  • The affected job advances through indexing to Ready.

How to verify the fix

  • The affected job advances through indexing to Ready.

What not to do

  • Do not delete retained task data or repeat an operation with an unknown outcome.

Technical notes

  • Status checks do not replay tasks or modify source documents.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
